themes.name: Transition from teacher-centred to dialogic pedagogy
themes.description: Teachers describe moving away from teacher-led explanation toward dialogic, talk-based approaches such as Think-Pair-Share and mixed-ability group work, prompted by coaching and professional development.
supportingQuotes: Before the coaching and PD I was teaching in a more teacher centred way.
Children work together in mixed ability groups to find answers to questions about minutes / seconds.
Healery: Ng Ajau Think-Pair-Share

themes.name: Uneven student engagement and participation
themes.description: Observation notes repeatedly flag disengaged or lower-attaining students who are not fully included, with off-task behaviour and misconceptions going unaddressed.
supportingQuotes: weaker students seem to be at the back.
On one table some children seem consistently hard to engage, not all the children get the answer of 120 seconds.
Some students are not looking at board but this is not addressed.

themes.name: Professional development through coaching and self-assessment
themes.description: A structured PD framework of five domains, baseline self-assessment, and coaching conversations frames teachers' growth, with an ethos that increasing awareness can make progress feel uncertain.
supportingQuotes: The 5 domains are:Domain 1: Dialogic Teaching.
Sometimes, the more we learn, the more we feel that we know less.
Coaching Conversations Link

themes.name: Developing student oracy and reasoning in mathematics
themes.description: The intervention aims to build pupils' confidence and ability to explain, reason, and communicate mathematical ideas in structured spoken English.
supportingQuotes: I wanted to boost their confidence and improve their speaking skills when explaining and communicating with their friends in Math lesson.
Getting students to explain a concept in their own words in English.
Helping students use reasoning language to develop thinking.

themes.name: Lack of lesson clarity and structure
themes.description: Observation notes reveal uncertainty about whether lesson objectives are communicated to students and limited questioning during instruction.
supportingQuotes: Not sure the Lesson Objective is clear to students.
It's not referred to again.
Questions mostly teacher-student but not many questions yet.

themes.name: Structured, Standards-Based Lesson Planning
themes.description: The documents follow a highly formalised lesson plan template aligned to national curriculum standards, specifying learning area, content standard, learning standard, timed sessions and Pdpc activities for a Year 4A class.
supportingQuotes: Content Standard 2.2 Decimals
Learning Standard 2.2.3. Multiply decimals by one-digit number, 10, 100 and 1000 with the product up to three decimal places.
SESSION 1 (60 Minutes | 0700 – 0800)

themes.name: Focus on Decimal Operations
themes.description: The mathematical content centres on multiplying and dividing decimals by one-digit numbers and powers of ten, with products and quotients limited to three decimal places, progressing from multiplication to division across lessons.
supportingQuotes: Multiply decimals by one-digit number, 10, 100 and 1000 with the product up to three decimal places.
Divide decimals by one-digit number, 10, 100 and 1000, and the quotient up to three decimal places.
Place the decimal point accurately in the quotient.

themes.name: Explicit Mathematical Vocabulary Instruction
themes.description: Key terminology such as decimal, dividend, divisor and quotient is deliberately taught through definition displays, a vocabulary word search, and pupil vocabulary videos, treating language as central to learning decimal operations.
supportingQuotes: Identify and explain key vocabulary related to decimal division.
The teacher introduces the lesson and displays the following mathematical vocabulary and definitions on whitebo
In 24 ÷ 6 = 4, 24 is the dividend.

themes.name: Measurable Objectives and Success Criteria
themes.description: Learning objectives and success criteria are expressed in quantified, criterion-referenced terms, targeting a specific proportion of pupils achieving a set pass rate, and requiring pupils to explain, solve, justify and self-check their work.
supportingQuotes: At The End Of The Lesson, 20/26 Pupils Are Able To;
Complete at least 4 out of 5 questions correctly.
Justify their answers during class discussion.

themes.name: Real-Life Contexts and Multimedia Engagement
themes.description: Lessons open by linking decimals to everyday experiences such as item prices in Ringgit Malaysia, supported by digital slides, videos and Google Drive resources that mediate the learning activities.
supportingQuotes: Teacher displays pictures (slide) showing prices of items (e.g., RM2.50, RM3.75, RM4.20).
Where do we see decimals in daily life?
IMG_8282 vocabulary.MOV

themes.name: Structured professional development and coaching architecture
themes.description: The data evidences a formalized CPD program built on baseline self-assessment across five named domains, a tiered 1-4 scoring rubric, and time-bounded PD sessions and group/individual coaching cycles.
supportingQuotes: The 5 domains are:Domain 1: Dialogic Teaching.
Each PD is a maximum of 2 hours.
You will meet once a month as a group of coachees with your coach for a maximum of 1 hour.

themes.name: Dialogic teaching and English-mediated classroom talk
themes.description: The self-assessed skills centre on orchestrating classroom talk in English: students explaining concepts in their own words, using reasoning language, and pre-teaching vocabulary through talk.
supportingQuotes: Getting students to explain a concept in their own words in English.
Knowing which vocabulary to pre-teach before a lesson and how to teach it through talk.
Planning talk activities that build understanding of concepts

themes.name: Interactive formative assessment through digital tools
themes.description: WhatsApp screenshots capture live quiz-based questioning in a science lesson, with the teacher posing multiple-choice items and giving immediate, affirming feedback to pupils.
supportingQuotes: What are animals with backbones called?
Select one A. Invertebrates B. Vertebrates
Great!!! So the answer is vetebrates

themes.name: STEM pedagogy aligned with national policy goals
themes.description: A presentation explicitly links Malaysian Ministry of Education macro-goals (DSTIN 2021-2030) to everyday classroom practice, foregrounding inquiry/PBL, formative assessment tools, and preparation for future STEM careers.
supportingQuotes: Connect the Malaysian Ministry of Education's macro-goals (DSTIN 2021-2030) to daily classroom impact.
Deconstruct the 7 core characteristics of STEM pedagogy and the evolving role of the teacher.
Your classroom practice directly fuels the nation's innovation economy.

themes.name: Reflective awareness and humility in professional growth
themes.description: A recurring framing message normalizes non-linear progress, presenting deepening professional awareness as the reason practitioners may feel they know less as they learn more.
supportingQuotes: It is not expected that you progress in everything.
Sometimes, the more we learn, the more we feel that we know less.
That's because we are more aware of what we are doing.

themes.name: Cross-Curricular Integration of STEM and English
themes.description: Learning is deliberately planned across Mathematics, Science, Design and Technology (RBT), and English, with science content serving as a vehicle for language development. This integration appears both in the carnival programme structure and in lesson plans where science topics anchor vocabulary work.
supportingQuotes: CROSS-CURRICULAR HANDS-ON LEARNING CARNIVAL: MATHEMATICS, SCIENCE, DESIGN AND TECHNOLOGY (RBT), AND ENGLISH THROUGH THE SCIENCE KIT LOAN PROGRAMME AT SK NANGA AJAU, BETONG FOR THE YEAR 2026

themes.name: Hands-On, Station-Based Experiential Learning
themes.description: Learning is organised around physical, manipulative activities at timed booths and challenges, emphasising doing, building, and investigating rather than passive instruction. Activities include puzzles, experiments, and design challenges across multiple science topics.
supportingQuotes: Organ assembly puzzle
Foil boat design challenge
Ramp experiment

themes.name: English-Medium Science Instruction and Vocabulary Development
themes.description: Science is taught through English (DLP) with explicit vocabulary objectives, sentence building, and pronunciation targets embedded in science lessons. Language and content goals are planned together rather than separately.

themes.name: Higher-Order Thinking and Scientific Inquiry
themes.description: Activities and learning standards consistently promote prediction, testing, observation, analysis, and justification with evidence. HOTS questions and inquiry-based tasks require pupils to reason scientifically rather than merely recall facts.
